newsitem.title: UK: Canada bonds outclass rest in latest week - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds outclass rest in latest week - Salomon.

text.p: Canadian bonds were top dog among government debt markets in the latest week, according to data released by Salomon Brothers on Friday.

Prompted higher by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged, Canadian bonds outclassed Treasuries and gained 1.31 perent in local currency terms, well ahead of the index as a whole.
Chirpy Italian bonds came a close second, gaining 1.19 percent in lire as inflation data showed prices were heading lower and hopes rose that the government would push through a tough budget.

In the U.S., Tuesday's rate decision came as a surprise to some, and allowed Treasuries a sigh of relief. The market rose 1.12 percent as investors pushed their expectations for tighter monetary policy further down the line.
Salomon's world governemnt bond index rose 0.73 percent in local currencies and 0.48 percent in dollars.
In core Europe, the benchmark Bund market put in a meagre performance in local currency terms, adding 0.53 percent, and an even poorer performance in dollar terms with a gain of just 0.02 percent.

But Europe's high-yielders took after Italy, with Swedish bonds adding 1.07 percent in crowns and Spain's Bonos adding 0.94 percent in pesetas. The two markets slotted into fourth and fifth place in the Salomon's index.
Analysts said a strong U.S. dollar also helped peripheral European markets.

In Britain, where a political split over European Economic and Monetary Union opened up within the ruling Conservative Party, gilts gained 0.65 percent in sterling, falling just short of French OATs which added 0.68 percent in francs.
Japanese government bonds were the week's only losers in local currency terms, shaving 0.03 percent off in yen.
In dollar terms, Japan lost 1.03 percent but was kept company in negative terriroty by Switzerland and Finland, who lost 0.38 and 0.08 percent, respectively.
Dutch, Belgian and Austrian bonds held up with the core of Europe with returns of 0.70, 0.83 and 0.55 percent in local currency terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
